summary: Press anywhere in the timeline and it takes the keyboard, with a thin blue ring round the dock to show it: J/K/L shuttle, I and O mark, the arrows step frames and edit points, Command-K splits, Home and End go to the ends, B and V pick the Blade and Select. Click the picture and the canvas gets the keys back, so L is the Line tool again.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any screen recording.

try.do: With the clip picked, press the right arrow. The picture nudges a point, because the canvas has the keyboard.
Press Command-Z, then click the Select arrow in the timeline's own bar. A blue ring goes round the dock. Press the right arrow three times: the playhead steps three frames and the picture stays put.
Press Command-K to cut at the playhead, then Home, then the down arrow. The playhead lands on the cut you just made.
Press I, then End, Shift-left and O, then M. The green In to Out stretch and a marker appear on the ruler. Option-I and Option-O clear them one at a time.
Press Home, then L twice: it plays at double speed and the transport says 2x. K stops, J plays backwards.
Press B: the timeline's Blade lights up. V puts it back to Select.
Click the picture. The ring goes, and L picks the Line tool instead of playing.

evaluate: Is the thin ring round the dock enough to tell you which one the keys are talking to, or do you want it stronger?
Should the timeline take the keyboard by itself when a recording opens, so J/K/L work before any click?
Is Command-K for Split, with B picking up the Blade, the right trade now that B no longer cuts at the playhead on the timeline?
Does a silent shuttle at 2x and backwards bother you, or is picture-only fine for finding a moment?
rough: Sound only plays at normal speed forwards. Premiere plays pitched sound while shuttling at 2x and backwards; here those run silent.
A (Premiere's Track Select Forward) is not bound: the timeline cannot yet carry more than one clip in a drag. Filed as its own task; until then A on the timeline is still the Arrow tool.
E (Extend Edit) is not bound. Roll Edit to Playhead is on a cut's right-click menu.
The mock's K adds a key at the playhead; the task asked for K as Stop, so K is Stop on a focused timeline and Shift-K / Option-K still step between keys.
The focus ring is not in the mock. It is Premiere's focused-panel outline, added because the same letter now means two things.
The mock's transport has no speed readout; the 2x beside the time only shows while a shuttle runs faster, slower or backwards.
